type: national_forest_boundary (TR-NATIONAL-FOREST); act is a consolidation and renaming, not a boundary change
clauses: C1: consolidates the Natural Bridge National Forest (Proc. Sept. 12, 1927, 45 Stat. 2924) with the George Washington National Forest (Proc. Jan. 28, 1927, 44 Stat. 2633); the combined area is known as the George Washington National Forest.
C2: declares that the order neither gives national-forest status to any publicly owned land nor removes it (interpretive limit on C1).
status_leaning: yes, if any former Natural Bridge lands remain in the George Washington National Forest today

end_or_current_basis.date_or_interval: 1936-04-21 for the former Natural Bridge lands placed in the Jefferson National Forest; open for any former Natural Bridge lands not so placed
end_or_current_basis.mechanism: later proclamation reserved part of the consolidated lands as a new forest (Jefferson NF, 'Natural Bridge Division'), ending C1's naming effect for those lands

savings: None needed for a consolidation; C2 preserves the prior status of all lands. FLPMA s.701 not relevant (national-forest status, not a withdrawal under FLPMA review).
contrary_evidence_checked: Proclamation 2165 preamble says it includes 'lands heretofore forming parts of the George Washington National Forest'; its Natural Bridge Division runs along the James River from North River (Glasgow) to Rocky Point Ferry, south and west of the river (APP text via WebFetch).
Forest History Society chronology: 'Natural Bridge (VA) [transferred to George Washington, 1933]'; no record of what part later went to Jefferson.

Whether the 1927 Natural Bridge NF included lands north and east of the James River (Amherst County, today's Pedlar district of the GWNF) was NOT established; Wikipedia, Sherpa Guides and Proclamation 1695 (1924, boundaries by diagram only) do not say.

Held APP corpus also lists the NRA silk-and-rayon order of the same date as 6210; the clause-drafts copy labels it 6210-A, and the printed copy closes '[No. 6210]' on the consolidation order. Identity is the consolidation order.
missing_evidence: Boundary diagram of the Natural Bridge NF proclamation of Sept. 12, 1927 (45 Stat. 2924) compared with the Natural Bridge Division of Proclamation 2165 (49 Stat. 3506): shows whether any Natural Bridge lands stayed in the GWNF.
Current GWNF/Jefferson NF proclaimed-boundary record (Forest Service Lands status or 'Establishment and Modification of National Forest Boundaries' table, FS-612).
end_found_via: web search (APP proclamation text, Wikipedia, Forest History Society chronology); held data had no edge or reverse citation
reusable: A per-forest chain of proclamations (USFS FS-612 'Establishment and Modification of National Forest Boundaries and Names') would decide this and every other forest boundary/renaming order in one lookup.

type: land_withdrawal_general in substance (TR-LAND-WITHDRAWAL); X1 typed it national_forest_boundary (type mismatch: it is a temporary withdrawal for classification pending possible forest inclusion)
clauses: C1: temporarily withdraws NW1/4NW1/4 sec. 6 and NE1/4SW1/4 sec. 8, T. 2 N., R. 2 W., Louisiana meridian, from settlement, location, sale or entry, for classification and pending determination whether to include them in a national forest (Pickett Act, 36 Stat. 847, as amended 37 Stat. 497), subject to valid existing claims.
C2: own term: in force 'unless and until revoked by the President or by act of Congress'.

end_or_current_basis.mechanism: standing withdrawal; no revoking EO, PLO or statute found
end_or_current_basis.citation: FederalRegister.gov full-text API (1994 on) and held corpus reverse-citation scan: no instrument naming EO 5511 or 'December 11, 1930' as revoked

savings: FLPMA s.701 (Pub. L. 94-579) continues the withdrawal until modified (continuity point, not an end). Valid existing claims excepted by the order itself.
contrary_evidence_checked: Kisatchie NF Proclamation 2173 (June 3, 1936) reserves acquired lands of the Catahoula, Evangeline, Kisatchie and Vernon divisions by diagram; it does not name these tracts or EO 5511. Inclusion in the forest, if it happened, would complete the purpose but would not by itself revoke the order (ruling 3: an endpoint needs a reason).
EO 6629 (1934) Louisiana classification withdrawals list other townships, not R. 2 W.
No hit in 1994-2026 Federal Register; pre-1994 Public Land Orders not searched (no index held or reachable).
missing_evidence: BLM MLRS (successor to LR2000) case/withdrawal record for T. 2 N., R. 2 W., Louisiana meridian, secs. 6 and 8.
Index of pre-1994 Public Land Orders for Louisiana (BLM PLO tables; FR 1942-1993).
Master title plat / GLO tract book for those 80 acres (patent or inclusion in the Evangeline division would show what happened to the land).
end_found_via: no end found; search: held reverse-citation scan, FederalRegister.gov API, web search
reusable: Status of small Pickett Act tracts turns on BLM land-status records keyed by township/range/section; a cached MLRS/master-title-plat lookup by legal description would serve every general withdrawal.

type: administrative-site withdrawal (X1: national_forest_boundary; TR-NATIONAL-FOREST covers administrative sites; TR-LAND-WITHDRAWAL equally applicable, since the land lies outside the forest)
order_date: 1932-02-15 (held texts; X1 EVENT_CANDIDATES gives 1932-02-13, a discrepancy to fix)
clauses: C1: withdraws N1/2NW1/4 sec. 14, T. 16 N., R. 20 E., Mount Diablo meridian, Nevada (80 acres) and reserves it for the Department of Agriculture as the McClellan Peak lookout site for administration of the Tahoe National Forest, subject to valid existing rights.
C2: own term: until revoked by the President or by act of Congress.

end_or_current_basis.mechanism: standing withdrawal; no revoking EO, PLO or statute found
end_or_current_basis.citation: FederalRegister.gov API 1994-2026 ('McClellan Peak': 0 hits); held reverse-citation scan: no citing instrument

savings: FLPMA s.701 continuity; valid existing rights excepted by the order.
contrary_evidence_checked: PLO 7873 (83 FR 44654, Aug. 31, 2018, Nevada) checked: does not include T. 16 N., R. 20 E.
PLO 7286/7289 page (62 FR, Oct. 9, 1997) checked: not relevant.
Possible transfer of Nevada administration from Tahoe NF to Toiyabe NF and abandonment of the lookout would not by themselves end the withdrawal (ruling 3).
missing_evidence: BLM MLRS record or master title plat for T. 16 N., R. 20 E., MDM, sec. 14.
Pre-1994 Nevada PLO index (FR 1942-1993).
end_found_via: no end found; held scan, FR API, web search
reusable: Same land-status lookup as EO 5511; lookout/administrative-site withdrawals were often revoked in batches by 1950s-1970s PLOs, so a pre-1994 PLO index keyed by 'Executive Order of <date>' would resolve many at once.

type: military_naval_reservation (TR-MILITARY-RESERVATION); outlier: the lands were already in the Chugach National Forest (two lifecycles)
clauses: C1: reserves about 82 acres on Cordova Point, Orca Inlet, Prince William Sound, Alaska, for naval purposes, subject to existing private rights, and places them under the Navy Department.

end_or_current_basis.mechanism: rescission by later executive order; area restored to its former national-forest status
end_or_current_basis.instrument: EO 4204 (Apr. 15, 1925): 'The Executive Order (No. 1237) of August 15, 1910 ... is hereby rescinded and the said area ... restored to its former National Forest status'

savings: None in EO 4204. The restoration returns the land to Chugach NF status; that consequence belongs to EO 4204 and the forest proclamations, not to EO 1237.
contrary_evidence_checked: No edge in later-events EDGES.csv (that file covers OFR disposition notes, 1937 on, only).
No sign of a later re-reservation reviving EO 1237 (a new reservation would be a new instrument).
Scan text is OCR of a State Department true copy; EO 4204 repeats the metes and bounds of EO 1237 exactly, which confirms identity.
missing_evidence: Codebook grading of the ProQuest replica scans (both texts are archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook).
end_found_via: held corpus reverse-citation scan (number pattern 'Order (No. 1237)'); not in EDGES.csv
reusable: Reverse-citation index over all held texts (number and date patterns) found this end in seconds.

type: military_naval_reservation (TR-MILITARY-RESERVATION); enlargement of Fort Armstrong, Hawaii (territorial lands; Organic Act s.91 and Admission Act s.5 are leads)
clauses: C1: with the consent of the Governor of the Territory of Hawaii, withdraws and sets aside for military purposes a tract of 80,170 sq. ft. (1.84 acres) at Kaakaukukui, Kakaako, Honolulu, bounded by Bishop Estate land, the Fort Armstrong Military Reservation, and Territory lands, beside Ala Moana and the Kawaiahao ditch.
status_leaning: no (the Fort Armstrong site is now Honolulu Harbor and Kakaako state lands), but no instrument for this tract was found

end_or_current_basis.mechanism: piecemeal restoration and transfer of Fort Armstrong to the Territory/State of Hawaii
end_or_current_basis.instrument: Merged into the consolidated description of EO 5487 (Nov. 14, 1930), which recites EO 2901. Later partial disposals found: EO 9861 (1947, road parcels from EO 2323/2335 lands), transfer of a quarantine-station portion to the Federal Works Agency under 63 Stat. 177 (1949), EO 10309 (Dec. 3, 1951; two tracts of 0.82 and 1.66 acres, conditional), EO 10597 and EO 10603 (1955). None is shown to cover the 1918 tract.

savings: Organic Act s.91 restorations return ceded land to the Territory; EO 10309 conditions precedent (Army certification) delay any transfer it covers.
contrary_evidence_checked: EO 5487 recites EO 2901 as one of the orders forming Fort Armstrong; its Tract 1 includes courses along the sewer pumping station and drainage ditch that match EO 2901's courses (Ala Moana, ditch).
Wikipedia: Army abandoned the fort by 1950; Corps of Engineers stayed until 1974; site now container port.
UH Hawaii Congressional Papers timeline: first Admission Act s.5(e) surplus transfers in 1962, locations unnamed.
missing_evidence: Instrument conveying the remainder of Fort Armstrong Tract No. 1 (EO 5487) after 1955: Army/GSA deed, Hawaii Admission Act s.5(e) conveyance record, or a later executive order.
Survey overlay of the EO 2901 courses on the EO 5487, EO 10309 and EO 10597 tracts.
end_found_via: held reverse-citation scan found EO 5487 and the Fort Armstrong chain; web search for the post-1955 disposal failed
reusable: A reservation-level chain file (all orders naming 'Fort Armstrong') built once from held texts would serve every Fort Armstrong order (EO 1008, 1175, 1362, 1559, 2323, 2335, 2464, 2901, 5487, 9861, 10309, 10597, 10603).

type: indian_reservation_trust, sub-pattern (b) reservation addition (TR-INDIAN-RESERVATION). Held APP file title 'Camp McDowell Reservation, Arizona' is wrong; the text is the Navajo addition
clauses: C1: withdraws from sale and settlement a described tract in Arizona and New Mexico Territories and sets it apart as an addition to the Navajo Reservation.
C2: proviso: does not affect existing valid rights.

end_or_current_basis.date_or_interval: Arizona portion: current, now within the statutory exterior boundaries of 1934. New Mexico portion: ended in parts on 1908-12-30 and 1911-01-16.
end_or_current_basis.mechanism: Arizona: continuing reservation, confirmed and made permanent by statute. New Mexico: restorations to the public domain by later orders.
end_or_current_basis.instrument: EO 744 (Jan. 28, 1908) redescribed the addition to remove the Jicarilla conflict (amendment; continuity). EO 1000 (Dec. 30, 1908) restored unallotted NM lands in T. 17-23 N., R. 5-8 W., except 110 unapproved allotments. EO 1284 (Jan. 16, 1911) restored the remaining unallotted NM lands west of the first guide meridian. EO 1995 (July 23, 1914) released sec. 10, T. 24 N., R. 29 E. (Ariz.) for a militia rifle range, to revert when no longer needed. Act of June 14, 1934, ch. 521, 48 Stat. 960, defines the Arizona exterior boundary (south line between T. 20 and 21 N.) and permanently withdraws 'all temporary withdrawals of public lands in Arizona heretofore made for Indian purposes by Executive order or otherwise'.
end_or_current_basis.citation: Held: IR1912 texts for 1908-01-28, 1908-12-30, 1911-01-16, 1911-05-24; wikisource EO_744, EO_1000, EO_1284; APP EO 1995. Not held: 48 Stat. 960 (read on GovInfo).

savings: C2 valid existing rights; the 1934 Act saves 'all valid rights and claims initiated under the public land laws prior to approval'. NM allotments excepted by EO 1000 keep separate trust lifecycles. EO 1359 (May 24, 1911) re-reserved some NM lands restored by EO 1284 for Indian purposes (separate order).
contrary_evidence_checked: Whether the 1934 Act ends EO 709 by statutory supersession: the Act confirms boundaries and makes the withdrawal permanent without revoking earlier orders; TR-INDIAN-RESERVATION treats such statutes as independent bases. Treated as continuity, with the statute as the controlling current basis.
The 1908 description wraps the south and east of the 1882 Hopi reservation and does not overlap it, so the Hopi partition statutes do not reach these lands.
EO 1995 rifle-range reverter: whether it reverted is unknown, but it affects one section only.
missing_evidence: Held copy of 48 Stat. 960 (Statutes at Large or GovInfo PDF) for the quotation.
A tract comparison confirming every Arizona township of the EO 744 description lies inside the 1934 boundary.
end_found_via: held corpus (Wikisource 'Amended by' notes, IR1912 compilation, reverse-citation scan) plus web for the 1934 statute
reusable: The 1912 GPO Indian-reservation compilation (held) gives the whole chain per reservation; adding Kappler vol. IV-V and the 1934-era confirming statutes would close most Indian reservation additions.

clauses: C1: under s.5 of the Act of Feb. 8, 1887, extends for ten years the trust period on allotments to Indians of the Devils Lake Reservation, North Dakota, whose trust period expires during calendar year 1923.

end_or_current_basis.date_or_interval: within calendar year 1933 (each allotment on the tenth anniversary of its 1923 expiry date)
end_or_current_basis.mechanism: own terms (fixed ten-year extension expired); succeeded, not superseded, by a further extension
end_or_current_basis.instrument: Own text; EO 5953 (Nov. 23, 1932) extended Devils Lake trusts expiring in 1933 for ten years 'from the respective dates of expiration'

savings: Trust title is an accrued statutory effect; later extensions (EO 5953; then IRA s.2, 48 Stat. 984, if Devils Lake was covered) carry the trust forward under their own authority.
contrary_evidence_checked: Allotments fee-patented before 1933 (for example competency patents under the Burke Act of 1906) left the trust earlier; this changes the end only for those allotments.
EO 5953 runs from the 1933 expiration and does not revive EO 3853.
IRA s.2 (June 18, 1934) came after the 1933 expiry, so it does not extend EO 3853's own period.
missing_evidence: Codebook grading of the replica scan; individual allotment expiry dates if a day-level end is wanted.
end_found_via: own text plus held corpus grep for 'Devils Lake' (EO 5303, 5768, 5953)
reusable: A table of trust-extension orders by reservation and expiry year (machine-built from held texts) closes every own-terms extension and shows its successor.

type: power_site_reserve (TR-POWER-SITE); outlier: the order is itself a restoration (Power-Site Restoration No. 481)
order_date: 1935-06-11 (APP and X1; the Hathi OCR prints 1936)
clauses: C1: revokes the Executive order of Dec. 12, 1912, creating Power-Site Reserve No. 325 (California), as to described lands in T. 5 N., R. 10 E. and T. 5 N., R. 11 E., Mount Diablo meridian.

end_or_current_basis.mechanism: spent on issue: a partial revocation of another order takes its whole effect on signing

savings: The order states no Federal Power Act s.24 condition or right of re-entry; none to carry. The restored lands' later status belongs to the public land laws and to any later withdrawal.
contrary_evidence_checked: Text states no own effective date, condition or reserved right.
A later re-withdrawal of the same lands would be a new instrument and would not revive EO 7069.
PSR 325's own remaining lands are a separate lifecycle (the 1912 order, EO 1661 era); not evaluated here.
end_found_via: own text (restoration orders are spent on issue)
reusable: Machine rule: title or text 'Restoration No.' or 'revoking in part' marks an order spent on issue; such orders can be closed in bulk and used as end evidence for their parent reserve.

type: lighthouse_reservation (TR-LIGHTHOUSE); outlier: the order is a restoration, and it was replaced
order_date: 1911-02-18 (EO 1311 recites 'February 18, 1911'; OCR of EO 1304 reads 'February z8')
clauses: C1: restores to the public domain for disposal under the general land laws 'section 1' (640.40 acres) and 'fractional section 11' (14.35 acres), reserved for lighthouse purposes by Executive Orders of Feb. 27, 1874 and June 12, 1900. The text names no township, range or state.

end_or_current_basis.mechanism: superseded by a replacement order issued 'in lieu of' it (EO 1304 lacked the township and state)
end_or_current_basis.instrument: EO 1311 (Mar. 1, 1911): 'in lieu of Executive Order No. 1304, dated February 18, 1911', restores sec. 1 and fractional sec. 11, T. 5 S., R. 14 W., Florida

savings: None. Any restoration effect belongs to EO 1311.
contrary_evidence_checked: Whether EO 1304 had any operative effect between Feb. 18 and Mar. 1, 1911: its land description is incomplete, and EO 1311 replaced it; even if it operated, a restoration is spent on issue.
Parent orders of Feb. 27, 1874 and June 12, 1900 are separate lifecycles ended in part by EO 1311.
missing_evidence: Codebook grading of the replica scans.
reusable: Reverse-citation index; 'in lieu of' is a supersession phrase worth a dedicated machine pattern.

type: public_water_reserve (TR-WATER-RESERVE); Public Water Reserve No. 155, Utah and Wyoming
clauses: C1 (Utah tract): SE1/4SW1/4 sec. 27, T. 32 S., R. 23 E., Salt Lake meridian, withdrawn and reserved for public use under s.10 of the Stock-Raising Homestead Act (39 Stat. 862, 865).
C2 (Wyoming tracts): N1/2NW1/4 sec. 12, T. 12 N., R. 104 W., and lots 8 and 9, sec. 11, T. 14 N., R. 106 W., Sixth P.M., same withdrawal.
C3: name 'Public Water Reserve No. 155, Utah and Wyoming'; subject to valid existing rights.

end_or_current_basis.date_or_interval: Wyoming tracts (C2): ended 1998-06-25. Utah tract (C1): current basis, checked 2026-10-28, no revocation found.
end_or_current_basis.mechanism: C2: partial revocation by Public Land Order; lands opened to the public land laws. C1: standing withdrawal.
end_or_current_basis.instrument: PLO 7330, 'Modification and Partial Revocation of 9 Executive Orders, 17 Secretarial Orders, and 8 Bureau of Land Management Orders; Wyoming': the Executive Order of June 15, 1934 creating Public Water Reserve No. 155 is 'hereby revoked insofar as' it affects T. 12 N., R. 104 W., sec. 12, N1/2NW1/4 and T. 14 N., R. 106 W., sec. 11, lots 8 and 9. Effective June 25, 1998.

savings: FLPMA s.701 continuity for C1. PLO 7330 opens lands 'subject to valid existing rights, the provisions of existing withdrawals, other segregations of record'.
contrary_evidence_checked: PLO 7261 (62 FR, May 21, 1997, Wyoming) checked: does not touch PWR 155.
FR full-text search for a Utah revocation of PWR 155 (1994-2026): none found.
PLO 7330 lists 'June 15, 1934' among revoked orders and names PWR 155, and its land list matches C2 exactly.
missing_evidence: Held copy of 63 FR 28516 (GovInfo PDF) to support the C2 end.
Utah tract: BLM MLRS record or pre-1994 Utah PLO index for T. 32 S., R. 23 E., SLM, sec. 27.
A printed government copy of EO 6740 (none held).
end_found_via: web search hit on PLO 7330, then GovInfo text; FederalRegister.gov API for the Utah check
reusable: A PLO table (number, date, FR cite, orders and reserve numbers revoked, lands) parsed from FR 1994-2026 and BLM PLO tables would resolve water reserves and power sites by reserve number.

type: land_withdrawal_general (TR-LAND-WITHDRAWAL); withdrawal in aid of proposed legislation
clauses: C1: temporarily withdraws S1/2 sec. 12, T. 21 N., R. 86 W., 6th P.M., Wyoming, from settlement, location, sale or entry, in aid of proposed legislation, subject to valid existing rights.
C2: own term: until revoked by the President or by act of Congress.

end_or_current_basis.mechanism: express revocation by later executive order, so that the Secretary of the Interior could withdraw the land under the Act of May 24, 1928 for an intermediate landing field
end_or_current_basis.instrument: EO 6679 (Apr. 16, 1934), 'Revocation of Executive Order No. 4810, of February 14, 1928, Withdrawing Public Land, Wyoming'

savings: None in EO 6679; the land passed to a new withdrawal under a different act (a new lifecycle, not EO 4810's).
contrary_evidence_checked: Lands match exactly (S1/2 sec. 12, T. 21 N., R. 86 W.).
No reinstatement found.
end_found_via: web search found the APP title; the revoking order was already held but absent from EDGES.csv
reusable: Reverse-citation index over held texts; EO titles beginning 'Revocation of Executive Order No.' can be harvested mechanically.

type: administrative site within a forest reserve (X1: land_withdrawal_general; TR-NATIONAL-FOREST administrative-site pattern fits better)
clauses: C1: declares and sets apart as a nursery site, under the Agriculture appropriation act of Mar. 3, 1905 (33 Stat. 872), SW1/4NE1/4, SE1/4NW1/4, NE1/4SW1/4 and NW1/4SE1/4 sec. 17, T. 2 S., R. 3 E., Salt Lake meridian, Utah, within the Salt Lake Forest Reserve.
C2: reserves the land from appropriation under any of the land laws.

end_or_current_basis.mechanism: standing reservation; the nursery closed about 1920 but no revoking instrument found
end_or_current_basis.citation: Held reverse-citation scan and FR search found no instrument naming the order; site history from Cottonwood Canyons Foundation 'Larch Tree History' (Wasatch Nursery beside Spruces Campground, Big Cottonwood Canyon, 1905/1906-1920)

savings: FLPMA s.701 continuity. The land also remains national-forest land (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF) under the forest proclamations, independent of this order.
contrary_evidence_checked: End of the nursery use in 1920 and conversion to a community camp in 1921 are not a revocation (ruling 3).
Identity of the site with the Wasatch Nursery rests on location (sec. 17, T. 2 S., R. 3 E. is in Big Cottonwood Canyon) and dates; an inference, not a recorded match.
missing_evidence: BLM MLRS or Forest Service land-status record for sec. 17, T. 2 S., R. 3 E., SLM.
Pre-1994 PLO index for Utah.
Forest Service R4 'Wasatch-Cache administrative facilities history' (chapter on nurseries) read in full; the web copy could not be downloaded.
end_found_via: no end found; web search identified the site's history
reusable: Same land-status lookup as EO 5511 and 5799; Forest Service regional facilities histories cover many administrative-site orders.
